title: ADHD in Adults: What It Really Looks Like
description: Adult ADHD is different from childhood ADHD. Symptoms, how it's diagnosed, treatment options, and why so many adults are getting diagnosed later in life.

content.text: You're not lazy, stupid, or undisciplined. You might have adult ADHD—a condition that looks very different in adults than the hyperactive kid stereotype. Here's what it actually looks like.
Many adults with ADHD were never diagnosed as children because:

items: Hyperactivity often decreases with age, leaving subtler symptoms

content.text: An estimated 4.4% of US adults have ADHD, but most are undiagnosed. The average age of adult diagnosis is 35-40.
content.citation: Kessler et al., American Journal of Psychiatry, 2006

content.text: What Adult ADHD Actually Looks Like

items: Can't start tasks, even important ones
Emotional dysregulation (quick to frustration, rejection sensitivity)
Difficulty focusing on boring things (can't start)
Easily distracted by thoughts, not just environment
Always needing to be doing something

content.text: ADHD overlaps with and is often mistaken for:

items: Autism (both involve executive dysfunction, sensory issues)

content.text: ADHD and anxiety/depression often co-occur. 50%+ of adults with ADHD have a comorbid condition.

items: Clinical interview about current symptoms and history
Review of childhood symptoms (symptoms must have started before age 12)
Stimulants (Adderall, Vyvanse, Ritalin) - most effective, 70-80% response rate
Non-stimulants (Strattera, Wellbutrin, Qelbree) - options if stimulants don't work
Medication works quickly - days, not weeks

content.text: If you've struggled your whole life with focus, follow-through, and feeling like you're not living up to your potential—it might not be a character flaw. ADHD is a neurodevelopmental condition that responds well to treatment. Getting diagnosed can be life-changing.
